camera._owner: projection = doc 11; range = doc 12 (report C-63). data/ui.json references these rows, never restates them.
camera._deleted: yaw_snap_deg, pan_damping, zoom_damping -> doc 12 (rotation_mode and gesture constants in data/ui.json)

lod._z2_derivation: Reports RR-12 and RR-14. At Z2 (D 420, pitch 62): h 370.8, r_near 52.1, r_far 411.9. On the 128 m chunk grid that is exactly THREE rows, originating at 52.1 / 180.0 / 308.0 m; a fourth row would originate at 436.0 m > r_far and cannot exist (the former row at r=412 was the far EDGE, not a row origin). Columns per row = ceil(w(r_far_of_row)/128) with w(r)=2*sqrt(r^2+h^2)*0.64706, applied as a PURE CEILING with no discretionary rounding (RR-14): w = 533.4 / 623.8 / 717.2 m -> ceil(4.167) / ceil(4.874) / ceil(5.603) -> 5 / 5 / 6 = 16 chunks. Rows A and B are inside the MEDIUM boundary r<=197.3 m, so tiers are 10 MEDIUM + 6 FAR + 0 NEAR; opaque = 10*10 + 6*3 = 118, total = 118 + 41 = 159 (165 with overlays). 16 is the FLOOR of the band: grid alignment against the view axis can add at most one column to each row, giving the hard band 16..19 chunks (159..182 calls) -- hence the asymmetric +3/-0 chunk tolerance in test 19 rather than a percentage or a symmetric window. The earlier 17-chunk / 169-call figure rounded row B's 4.874 up to 6 by judgement and double-counted the misalignment already carried by the band.

emissive._window_nits: Per-family emissive brightness (report 98 / render-polish q1). A plain number is still accepted and applies to every family; a {family: nits} object is read per bucket by CityView. The families are NOT equally bright at equal nits: window_color luma runs civic #E8F0FF 0.94 > commercial #CFE6FF 0.89 > tech 0.84 > residential #FFCE8A 0.83 > industrial 0.80, so a flat 3.2 pushed the cool-white office and civic bays past the glow's HDR threshold and they bloomed into solid white blocks at Z2 while the warm residential bays still read as individual windows. (NOTE, measured: the threshold in force is Godot's default 1.0, because EnvironmentController pushes glow_intensity/strength/bloom but not the presets' glow_hdr_threshold_day/night, glow_hdr_scale or glow_levels rows. Lowering it to the authored 0.78 was tried and makes the frame marginally BRIGHTER, so it is not the fix -- the fix is the nits below.) Equal-luma normalisation alone would give commercial 2.98; 2.4 goes further on purpose, because an office floor lit for cleaners at 21:00 SHOULD sit below a living room. This scales brightness only -- day_gate still decides how many cells light, so RenderStateModel.lit_window_count is untouched by every value here.
emissive._far_tier: far_energy_scale, far_cell_m, far_bay_m and far_mullion_duty are the FAR band shader's calibration knobs, added when the tier was actually wired to the renderer. A lit BAND covers 100% of its segment's width where a lit near-tier window covers only the pane inside its cell, so at equal nits the far tier out-emits the medium chunks in front of it and the LOD boundary reads as a lighting change; 0.98 is the coverage ratio that makes a far storey and a near storey emit the same average radiance, measured at the Z2 showcase pose, once far_mullion_duty has taken its own 0.72 out. far_cell_m 6.4 (two window bays) is the width of one hash segment along a facade -- doc 11 rejects the PER-WINDOW hash at this range because a 3.2 m cell is sub-pixel and crawls, but 6.4 m is ~23 px at 500 m and ~10 px at 1200 m, which is stable, and it is what gives a far tower runs of lit floors instead of one solid stripe per storey. far_bay_m / far_mullion_duty draw the wall BETWEEN the windows, which the near tier gets from its texture and the far tier has no texture for: a 3.2 m periodic strip at 72% duty, crossfaded to its own mean by fwidth() as it approaches a pixel wide. That crossfade is not optional -- a periodic sub-pixel pattern moires, which is the same failure the per-window hash was rejected for, and the mean it fades to is exactly what the sharp pattern integrates to, so structure disappears with no brightness step.

blackout._carrying_event: BlockDarkChanged{block_id, block_dark, powered_fraction, restore_order} -- emitted and named by doc 04 §4 (report C-38 + RR-1). The renderer subscribes to this name and to no event named DistrictDarkChanged.

occupancy_hour_curve._owner: doc 11 (report C-66). Art, not simulation. Multiplied by doc 02's structural occ_b in §2.7.1. Six [hour, value] keyframes per building family, linearly interpolated, wrapping at 24:00. Read as: fraction of occupied floor area showing light.

daynight._night_floor: Playtest 03:19 on the Fold 6 (report NIGHT-1): deep night rendered as an OFF panel -- the street grid, every unlit façade and every silhouette resolved to 0 between the lamp pools. The three night keys below were #050810/#080C18 sky over a 0.10 ambient energy applied to that same near-black sky, i.e. ~0.0003 of radiance reaching an unlit face. The fix is a FLOOR, not a flood, and it is spent in three places: (1) the night sky keys are lifted to a deep navy so the sky itself is a colour rather than a hole, (2) `ambient_color_night` + `ambient_sky_contribution_night` add an authored blue-grey moonlight ambient that does not depend on how dark the sky is, and (3) moon_energy carries enough directional light to MODEL the geometry, so a tower reads as two faces and a roof instead of one flat card. The blackout ceremony survives because none of the three touches the emissive windows, the lamp billboards or the ground pools: a dark block still loses 100% of its light and only keeps the moonlight every block has.

environment._fog_clamp: fog_depth_end_eff = min(profile.end, active_far_cull_m); fog_depth_begin_eff = min(profile.begin, 0.75 * fog_depth_end_eff). Enforces the §2.8 invariant across presets and governor knob positions (test 23).

weather._rain_box_scaling: The 90 m box is authored for Z0/Z1, where it comfortably overshoots the frame. At Z2 (camera 370.8 m up, ~717 m of ground across the far row) the same box is a 90 m square of rain in the middle of a dry city -- the single worst weather read in the game. RULING: scale the emitter box in XZ with camera distance, and DO NOT scale `amount`. Particle count therefore stays exactly flat across the zoom range (that is the density cap: the same drops spread over more ground, never more drops), and `amount_ratio` still rides precip01 alone, so nothing restarts -- rule 2 of weather_fx.gd survives. Y is deliberately NOT scaled: the fall height sets `lifetime`, and writing `lifetime` mid-storm re-ages the whole bed and pops.

streetlights._pole: POLE ART ONLY. The billboard / pool / omni system is tuned and the surface pass does not touch it. `pole_color` multiplies the galvanised prop page and the base-weathering ramp StreetlightView bakes into the pole's vertex colour, so it has to stay dark enough to silhouette against a lit pavement and light enough for the page's half-metre AO bands to survive the multiply.
streetlights._pool_scale: `pool_radius_m` is the MESH radius StreetlightView builds (its POOL_RADIUS const). The drawn pool is that times light_pool.gdshader's `pool_scale`, which the shader owns because widening the disc is a vertex-stage scale on a buffer the view uploads once — no rebuild, no new AABB. At the shipped 1.35 the effective radius is 8.1 m against the 32 m streetlight_spacing_m: the pools no longer quite touch, but each one now covers the full width of an 8 m carriageway plus its kerbs, so the avenue reads as a dotted line on a lit road instead of as isolated circles in black (report NIGHT-1). It stops there because at Z2 a pool is ~19 px of soft disc per metre of radius and a wider one turns the marketed skyline into bokeh; the continuous half of the street read is the ground's own night floor above. Wetness still adds its own +50% on top.
streetlights._pool_y_superseded: STREET-1: pool_y_m 0.06 sat UNDER the carriageway's 0.10 top and every pool in the game was depth-buried by the road it was lighting. StreetlightView now takes its height from road_surface.asphalt_top_m + kerb_height_m + lamp.pool_lift_m. This row is kept for a clone with no road_surface block.

power_infra._owner: doc 11's DISTRIBUTION layer, read by game/render/power_infra_model.gd and game/render/power_infra_view.gd. Doc 04 owns the grid; this block owns only what it LOOKS like. Nothing electrical lives here on purpose: the WARNING/CRITICAL bands are PowerGrid.OVERLAY_WARNING_R / OVERLAY_CRITICAL_R (§5.10), the hot-winding line is HAZARD[transformer][0], and the SEVERE band is SOLVED from §2.6's thermal + hazard rows by PowerInfraModel.severe_ratio() — retuning doc 04 moves the visuals with it and there is no second copy to forget.
power_infra._scope: Pads and service drops only. Substations and plants are BUILDINGS (report 98 C-30) and CityView has drawn them since Wave 6; adding a second representation of them here would put two objects on one tile.
power_infra._pad: The cabinet is 204 triangles on ONE shared mesh, instanced city-wide. `pad_m` is the concrete apron, `cabinet_top_m` the crown of the lid (the smoke vent sits on it), and `riser_local_m` is where a service drop leaves the cabinet, in the pad's own local frame with +Z as the door face.
power_infra._fin_pitch: Seven fins across a 0.94 m radiator panel. The fins are shaded, not modelled (power_pad.gdshader): at Z0 one fin is ~3 px, which is the scale at which triangles cost and a periodic AO term does not.
power_infra._wires: NEAR only. `wire_fade_end_m` is BOTH the shader's fade-out distance and the CPU-side bucket gate in PowerInfraView, which is what makes the gate unobservable — a bucket is dropped only once every wire in it is already zero-width. `wire_min_px` holds a cable at ~1.4 screen px however far it is; without it a 45 mm wire is sub-pixel by 30 m and crawls. `wire_radius_m` is deliberately fatter than a real 20 mm triplex for the same reason.
power_infra._fade_derivation: 58 m is not 'somewhere inside NEAR' — it is the Z1 CAMERA HEIGHT, minus a margin. Doc 11 §2.5's Z1 pose is D 86.9 m at 48° pitch, so the camera sits 86.9·sin48 = 64.6 m above grade and NOTHING on the ground is within 58 m of it. The brief was 'visible when you look, never noisy at Z1+', and this is that sentence as a number: at Z0 (camera 10.1 m up, 14.9 m back) every wire in view is inside `wire_fade_begin_m` and fully drawn; by Z1 the layer is not merely faint but ZERO buckets submitted. Measured on the bench city: 4 wire buckets at Z0, 0 at Z1, 0 at Z2. 58 is also comfortably inside §2.5's 150 m NEAR boundary, so 'wires are a NEAR element' holds by construction instead of by mirroring the tier table into this view.
power_infra._wire_max_radius: A hard ceiling on the screen-space widening, in metres. It exists because the first cut sized the cable off `VIEWPORT_SIZE.y`, which COMPILES in a spatial vertex shader and reads 0 there on Forward Mobile: the shader's own `max(1.0, …)` guard then widened every service drop to ~130 m of near-opaque black and washed the entire screen at any close zoom. The height is now pushed in as a uniform (`PowerInfraView._sync_viewport_h`); this is the second lock, so no future plumbing mistake can repaint the screen.
power_infra._sag: Parabolic droop, capped. 5.5% of span is a slack service drop; the cap stops a 64 m L5 run (doc 04's largest service radius) from hanging 3.5 m into the street.
power_infra._distress: Smoke and sparks share ONE premultiplied-alpha MultiMesh (power_smoke.gdshader), so the whole distress layer is one draw call however bad the city gets, and the node is hidden entirely while nothing is in trouble. `puff_cap` is the city-wide billboard budget, spent worst-first; the governor's `particle_ratio` knob scales it and nothing else in this layer.
power_infra._smoke_value: Both greys are LIGHTER than a photograph of transformer smoke, and measured rather than chosen. Premultiplied alpha writes colour*a and takes (1-a) of the background, so the first pass (#292826 night / #7A7671 day at alpha 0.42) changed a night sky by about two per cent and landed within four per cent of the asphalt by day: 132 live billboards and NOTHING visible in either screenshot. A plume has to be lighter than what is behind it or it is not a plume, and a real one is, because it scatters.
power_infra._ramps: Render seconds. The char ramp is asymmetric on purpose: a failure is an EVENT and lands in half a second, a repair is a crew leaving and washes clean over two and a half — the player asked to see the fix land, and a step change reads as a glitch.
power_infra._polling: Render seconds. The topology pass walks every attached building (1,500 on the bench city) and runs only when the grid's shape moved; the state poll is 144 rows and is what a smoking transformer needs. PowerInfraFeed.signature() catches a roster that grew or shrank on the next state poll, and the shell can force a rebuild the same frame with note_topology_changed().

ground._owner: doc 11 §2.1's ground surfaces, ART side. `GroundSurface` reads this block and nothing else does; the shader constants stay in `weather`. The page set is tools/gen_textures.py's `ground_*`.
ground._districts: A district is doc 09's 1-4 contiguous blocks and carries a `color_index` 0..3 (data/starter_city.json `districts`). The renderer spends that index on GROUND TONE and on nothing else: the same pavement page, trimmed a few per cent in value and hue per district, so a player reading the skyline can still tell Downtown's pale slabs from Foundry Flats' oiled yard without a legend, an outline or a second texture in VRAM. A block with no district (every unbought block at t0) takes `undeveloped_tint`, which is why the city edge reads as scrub and the owned core reads as pavement.
ground._night_floor: report NIGHT-1. `night_color` is the cool skyglow tint both terms are spent in — a sodium-and-window blue-grey, not white, so a lifted street still reads as NIGHT. `*_albedo_lift` raises the surface's reflectance so the moonlight ambient actually bounces off it; `*_glow` is a small emission, the scattered city light a real street sits under, and it is the term that survives ambient going to zero. The ROAD row is roughly twice the terrain's: that ratio is the whole point, because a flat lift on both would brighten the frame without drawing the GRID. Wet roads take `night_glow_wet_mult` of the glow — a wet carriageway mirrors the skyglow away from the camera and the §2.9 lamp smear becomes the read instead.
ground._tone_calibration: Measured on the showcase's four-quadrant ground at 120 m, hour 13. The first draft (#8E9089/#98948E/#7C8A8C/#8C8378) was invisible across the avenue: four greys a few per cent apart, which is a tone nobody can name. These keep the SAME luma band (every one within 0.06 of developed_tint's 0.527, so no district reads as brighter ground) and spend the difference on HUE instead - cool slate, warm limestone, green-grey, oiled brown. That is the split the eye actually resolves at 80-200 m, and it stays a trim: put any two side by side against a road and they are still one city.

road_surface._owner: doc 11 §2.1.2 — the REAL STREET pass. `RoadSurfaceView` reads this block and nothing else does; `StreetlightPlacer` reads the `lamp` sub-block. The `ground` block above still owns the block interiors and the night floor the road inherits (`road_night_*`), which is why nothing here duplicates those numbers.
road_surface._geometry: One tile is 8 m. A single-tile street spends 2 x 1.40 m on kerb-and-footway and the remaining 5.20 m on two 2.60 m lanes. A single-tile avenue spends 2 x 1.05 m and gets two 2.95 m lanes. The starter city's avenues are TWO tiles wide (data/starter_city.json lays Slacum Ave down as x=15 AND x=16), so each half carries its own 1.05 m footway on the OUTER side only and 6.95 m of carriageway: two 3.475 m lanes running the same way, a white dashed lane divider between them, and half of the double-yellow at the shared edge. That is the whole reason `pair` exists in the packing below - per-tile guesswork would have drawn a centre line down the middle of each half and put a kerb in the middle of a 16 m avenue.
road_surface._sidewalk_night: Sits between the terrain floor (0.10 / 0.012) and the carriageway's (0.34 / 0.048), and just under the road's on purpose. Matching the terrain leaves a black gap either side of a lit carriageway - measured at the first draft's 0.22 / 0.030, where the footway read as darker than the lot behind it at 03:00. Matching the ROAD erases the kerb line, which is the edge this whole pass exists to draw. The gap between the two is the read.
road_surface._markings: Paint is drawn in the fragment stage from world metres, not from geometry: a dash phase taken off the WORLD coordinate runs continuously across tile seams for free, and 15 cm of line at Z0 costs no instances at all. `marking_night_glow` is the retroreflective read - real thermoplastic throws headlights and lamp light straight back, and it is the cheapest thing on this list that makes a night street legible.
road_surface._wear: All four terms are procedural and cost no texture memory: `patch_gain` is the 11 m mottle of an asphalt that has been cut and patched, `seam_darken` the joint where two 8 m pours meet, `wheel_path_gain` the polished tracks a lane's traffic wears into it, `gutter_darken` the grime that collects against a kerb. `wear_tile_gain` is the per-tile trim off INSTANCE_CUSTOM.a so two neighbouring pours are never the same grey.

lamp._owner: `StreetlightPlacer`. Derived from the road GRAPH, never from a tile parity test: a lamp stands ON a kerb the classification says exists, faces the carriageway, and alternates sides down a corridor at `spacing_tiles` - instead of stippling a diagonal across the whole city and standing every pole in open traffic. `spacing_tiles` 4 IS the authored `world.streetlight_spacing_m` of 32 m; the two halves of a dual carriageway each light every 8 tiles, staggered, so the avenue's effective pitch is the same 32 m off alternating kerbs.
lamp._corner_lamps: A lamp wherever a road tile carries TWO ADJACENT footways — the head of a cul-de-sac, the inside of a street corner. Deliberately NOT 'a lamp on each corner of a junction': a one-tile junction has three or four road neighbours and therefore at most ONE kerb, so it has no corner to stand a pole on, and its approaches are already lit at `spacing_tiles`. Standing one in the box anyway would put a pole in a traffic lane, which is the exact defect this pass exists to remove.
lamp._pool_lift: The ground pool used to be uploaded at base + 0.07 m while the road slab's TOP is at 0.10 m: every pool was depth-buried under the carriageway it was supposed to light, and what survived was the ring of it that spilled onto the block either side - which is exactly the 'streetlights look like sticks' read. It now rides just over the FOOTWAY (the highest thing under a lamp), so one disc covers kerb, gutter and both lanes.

water_surface._owner: doc 11 §2.1's third ground surface. main.gd builds the water tiles; GroundSurface.water() builds the material for them. Animated in the shader, never in script: a MultiMeshInstance3D of 15 quads cannot afford a per-frame CPU touch, and sc_time is already published for the window flicker.
water_surface._no_reflections: There is deliberately NO reflection probe here, at any preset. §2.11 gates the ONE probe the game may own to High and to the city at large; a second probe for a canal would double the cost of the feature that is already flagged for on-device validation. The sky read is a fresnel-weighted tint toward `sky_color`, which costs one dot product and lands within a few percent of a probe at these viewing angles.
water_surface._night: report NIGHT-1. 0.34 on top of a #0F2937 body put the canal at (0,0,11) — a black hole through the middle of the showcase. 0.50 plus the shader's night sky read (the fresnel term retargets onto `sc_fog_tint`) puts it back where a canal at night belongs: darker than the pavement either side of it, lighter than the sky, and still the coolest surface in the frame.

vehicles._promoted: The nine tuning knobs VehicleView shipped as script constants, promoted here so the vehicle look is data like everything else (report 98 / vehicle q5). Values are unchanged from the constants they replace.
vehicles._cast_shadows: OFF by default, i.e. on mobile (report 98 / vehicle q5). A vehicle layer's custom AABB is world-sized -- it has to be, because instances are written straight into the MultiMesh buffer and never update the auto AABB -- so every body layer intersects EVERY directional shadow split and is re-drawn once per split whether or not a single car is inside it. At balanced (2 splits) that is 7 extra draw calls for shadows nobody can see from 87 m up; at high (4 splits) it is 14, which High can afford and does. The per-preset `vehicle_shadows` row below overrides this key.

governor._owner: doc 11 §2.13, implemented by game/render/perf_governor.gd. The budget the ratios are taken against is 1000 / presets[active].target_fps, so a Performance device is judged at 33.3 ms and a Balanced one at 16.7 -- the governor never compares a phone against a budget its preset did not promise.
governor._thermal: doc 13 §2.8's statuses (PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_*, 0 NONE .. 6 SHUTDOWN), pushed through AndroidNative.thermal_status_changed. At/above thermal_block_up_status the governor stops stepping UP; at/above thermal_step_down_status it steps down on the next evaluation WITHOUT waiting out step_down_hold_s, because thermal headroom does not return by itself; at/above thermal_force_preset_status it latches the preset one rung down immediately. Cooling is hysteretic: a lower status only takes effect after thermal_recover_s at that status (doc 13 §2.8), so a device sitting on a boundary cannot oscillate. NOTE, flagged: doc 13 §2.8 also lists 'glow off' at SEVERE. glow_enabled is on `protected` above and doc 11 owns rendering, so the governor drops the preset instead and the signature moment survives.
